claim: H2A.Z is a universal mark of gene promoters, enhancers, and regulatory elements in eukaryotic chromatin.
source: The histone variant H2A.Z is a universal mark of gene promoters, enhancers, and regulatory elements in eukaryotic chromatin.
evidence: Supported by citations to prior work establishing this finding.

claim: SWR1 mediates site-specific incorporation of H2A.Z by a multi-step histone replacement reaction.
source: The chromatin remodeler SWR1 mediates site-specific incorporation of H2A.Z by a multi-step histone replacement reaction, evicting histone H2A-H2B from the canonical nucleosome and depositing the H2A.Z-H2B dimer.
evidence: Supported by citations to prior work and experimental data in the manuscript.

claim: SWR1 evicts histone H2A-H2B from the canonical nucleosome and deposits the H2A.Z-H2B dimer.
source: The chromatin remodeler SWR1 mediates site-specific incorporation of H2A.Z by a multi-step histone replacement reaction, evicting histone H2A-H2B from the canonical nucleosome and depositing the H2A.Z-H2B dimer.
evidence: Supported by citations to prior work and experimental data in the manuscript.

claim: Binding of both the canonical nucleosome and the H2A.Z-H2B dimer is essential for activation of SWR1.
source: Binding of both substrates, the canonical nucleosome and the H2A.Z-H2B dimer, is essential for activation of SWR1.
evidence: Supported by citations to prior work.

claim: SWR1 primarily recognizes key residues within the α2 helix in the histone-fold of nucleosomal histone H2A.
source: We found that SWR1 primarily recognizes key residues within the α2 helix in the histone-fold of nucleosomal histone H2A, a region not previously known to influence remodeler activity.
evidence: Supported by experimental data from hybrid nucleosome assays shown in Figure 1.

claim: The α2 helix in the histone-fold of nucleosomal histone H2A was not previously known to influence remodeler activity.
source: We found that SWR1 primarily recognizes key residues within the α2 helix in the histone-fold of nucleosomal histone H2A, a region not previously known to influence remodeler activity.
evidence: Based on the authors' knowledge of prior literature.

claim: SWR1 interacts preferentially with nucleosomal DNA at superhelix location 2 on the nucleosome face distal to its linker-binding site.
source: Moreover, SWR1 interacts preferentially with nucleosomal DNA at superhelix location 2 on the nucleosome face distal to its linker-binding site.
evidence: Supported by hydroxyl radical footprinting data shown in Figure 2.

claim: H2A.Z has an important role in transcriptional regulation.
source: The histone variant H2A.Z, a universal component of nucleosomes flanking eukaryotic promoters, enhancers, and other genetic elements, has an important role in transcriptional regulation (Santisteban et al., 2000; Albert et al., 2007; Barski et al., 2007).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior work.

claim: H2A.Z is a universal component of nucleosomes flanking eukaryotic promoters, enhancers, and other genetic elements.
source: The histone variant H2A.Z, a universal component of nucleosomes flanking eukaryotic promoters, enhancers, and other genetic elements, has an important role in transcriptional regulation (Santisteban et al., 2000; Albert et al., 2007; Barski et al., 2007).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior work.

claim: In Saccharomyces cerevisiae, H2A.Z is deposited by the ATP-dependent activity of the multi-component SWI/SNF-related SWR1 complex.
source: In Saccharomyces cerevisiae, H2A.Z is deposited by the ATP-dependent activity of the multi-component SWI/SNF-related SWR1 complex, which replaces nucleosomal histone H2A-H2B with H2A.Z-H2B in a coupled histone-dimer transfer (Mizuguchi et al., 2004; Luk et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior work.

claim: SWR1 replaces nucleosomal histone H2A-H2B with H2A.Z-H2B in a coupled histone-dimer transfer.
source: In Saccharomyces cerevisiae, H2A.Z is deposited by the ATP-dependent activity of the multi-component SWI/SNF-related SWR1 complex, which replaces nucleosomal histone H2A-H2B with H2A.Z-H2B in a coupled histone-dimer transfer (Mizuguchi et al., 2004; Luk et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior work.

claim: SWR1 recruitment to nucleosome-deficient or nucleosome-free regions (NFRs) of yeast promoters is due to its preference for nucleosomes adjoining long linker DNA.
source: SWR1 recruitment to nucleosome-deficient or nucleosome-free regions (NFRs) of yeast promoters is due to its preference for nucleosomes adjoining long linker DNA (Ranjan et al., 2013), but post-recruitment activation of the SWR1 complex requires binding of both its natural substrates—the canonical nucleosome and the H2A.Z-H2B dimer—which also serve as essential activators of SWR1 (Luk et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Post-recruitment activation of the SWR1 complex requires binding of both its natural substrates—the canonical nucleosome and the H2A.Z-H2B dimer.
source: SWR1 recruitment to nucleosome-deficient or nucleosome-free regions (NFRs) of yeast promoters is due to its preference for nucleosomes adjoining long linker DNA (Ranjan et al., 2013), but post-recruitment activation of the SWR1 complex requires binding of both its natural substrates—the canonical nucleosome and the H2A.Z-H2B dimer—which also serve as essential activators of SWR1 (Luk et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior work.

claim: The canonical nucleosome and the H2A.Z-H2B dimer serve as essential activators of SWR1.
source: SWR1 recruitment to nucleosome-deficient or nucleosome-free regions (NFRs) of yeast promoters is due to its preference for nucleosomes adjoining long linker DNA (Ranjan et al., 2013), but post-recruitment activation of the SWR1 complex requires binding of both its natural substrates—the canonical nucleosome and the H2A.Z-H2B dimer—which also serve as essential activators of SWR1 (Luk et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Progression of the SWR1-mediated reaction on the canonical 'AA' nucleosome generates the 'AZ' and 'ZZ' nucleosome states consecutively.
source: Progression of the SWR1-mediated reaction on the canonical 'AA' nucleosome generates the 'AZ' and 'ZZ' nucleosome states consecutively, which leads to repression of the ATPase and histone exchange activities of SWR1 by the H2A.Z-nucleosome end-product, thereby preventing futile expenditure of chemical energy (Luk et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior work.

claim: The H2A.Z-nucleosome end-product represses the ATPase and histone exchange activities of SWR1, thereby preventing futile expenditure of chemical energy.
source: Progression of the SWR1-mediated reaction on the canonical 'AA' nucleosome generates the 'AZ' and 'ZZ' nucleosome states consecutively, which leads to repression of the ATPase and histone exchange activities of SWR1 by the H2A.Z-nucleosome end-product, thereby preventing futile expenditure of chemical energy (Luk et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Specific α-C helix residues of H2A.Z on the free H2A.Z-H2B dimer are critical for its SWR1-activating function.
source: Specific α-C helix residues of H2A.Z on the free H2A.Z-H2B dimer are critical for its SWR1-activating function (Clarkson et al., 1999; Wu et al., 2005).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The key-activating elements of the canonical nucleosome that distinguish it from the non-activating H2A.Z-nucleosome have been obscure.
source: However, the key-activating elements of the canonical nucleosome that distinguish it from the non-activating H2A.Z-nucleosome have been obscure.
evidence: Based on the authors' knowledge of prior literature.

claim: The histone-fold, but not the α-C helix of histone H2A in the nucleosome, has a major role in the activation of the SWR1 complex.
source: Here, we show that the histone-fold, but not the α-C helix of histone H2A in the nucleosome, has a major role in the activation of the SWR1 complex.
evidence: Supported by experimental data from hybrid nucleosome assays shown in Figure 1.

claim: A local DNA site on the nucleosome core particle is critical for activating SWR1.
source: We also define a local DNA site on the nucleosome core particle that is critical for activating SWR1.
evidence: Supported by experimental data from DNA gap experiments shown in Figure 3.

claim: Interchanging the M6 and α-C regions of H2A with H2A.Z on the nucleosome had only a small effect on SWR1 activity.
source: Interchanging the M6 and α-C regions of H2A with H2A.Z on the nucleosome had only a small effect on SWR1 activity as measured by nucleosomal incorporation of H2A.Z-3xFlag, which generates a native gel mobility upshift (Figure 1A).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: An additional interchange of the M4 domain of nucleosomal H2A with H2A.Z caused a ∼90% decrease in H2A.Z replacement by SWR1.
source: Strikingly, an additional interchange of the M4 domain of nucleosomal H2A with H2A.Z caused a ∼90% decrease in H2A.Z replacement by SWR1, and extension of the interchange to M2 and M3 domains further reduced SWR1's activity (Figure 1A).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Extension of the interchange to M2 and M3 domains further reduced SWR1's activity.
source: Strikingly, an additional interchange of the M4 domain of nucleosomal H2A with H2A.Z caused a ∼90% decrease in H2A.Z replacement by SWR1, and extension of the interchange to M2 and M3 domains further reduced SWR1's activity (Figure 1A).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Interchanging the M4 domain alone caused a large reduction in activity of SWR1.
source: Interchanging the M4 domain alone caused a large reduction in activity of SWR1, and activity was also reduced by interchange of M5 and M3A domains individually, whereas M2 and M3B domain interchanges had minimal effects (Figure 1B,C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B,C.

claim: Activity of SWR1 was reduced by interchange of M5 and M3A domains individually.
source: Interchanging the M4 domain alone caused a large reduction in activity of SWR1, and activity was also reduced by interchange of M5 and M3A domains individually, whereas M2 and M3B domain interchanges had minimal effects (Figure 1B,C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B,C.

claim: M2 and M3B domain interchanges had minimal effects on SWR1 activity.
source: Interchanging the M4 domain alone caused a large reduction in activity of SWR1, and activity was also reduced by interchange of M5 and M3A domains individually, whereas M2 and M3B domain interchanges had minimal effects (Figure 1B,C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B,C.

claim: Residues contained entirely within the H2A histone-fold motif (the α1 helix, α2 helix, and loop 2) contribute to activation of SWR1.
source: Thus, residues contained entirely within the H2A histone-fold motif (the α1 helix, α2 helix, and loop 2) contribute to activation of SWR1.
evidence: Inferred from the experimental data showing effects of domain interchanges.

claim: The non-activating H2A.Z-nucleosome shows slightly decreased affinity for SWR1.
source: Underlying mechanism(s) could include improved enzyme binding, as the non-activating H2A.Z-nucleosome shows slightly decreased affinity for SWR1 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1), but activation at a post-recruitment step is required, because neither ATPase stimulation nor histone replacement occurs under saturating conditions ([Luk et al., 2010] and data not shown).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Activation at a post-recruitment step is required, because neither ATPase stimulation nor histone replacement occurs under saturating conditions.
source: Underlying mechanism(s) could include improved enzyme binding, as the non-activating H2A.Z-nucleosome shows slightly decreased affinity for SWR1 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1), but activation at a post-recruitment step is required, because neither ATPase stimulation nor histone replacement occurs under saturating conditions ([Luk et al., 2010] and data not shown).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior work and unpublished data.

claim: Interchange of the M4 region of H2A for H2A.Z (substitution of five residues) in yeast causes lethality.
source: Interchange of the M4 region of H2A for H2A.Z (substitution of five residues) in yeast causes lethality (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claim: The N-terminal portion of the H2A α2 helix provides an essential function apart from regulating SWR1 activity.
source: This indicates that the N-terminal portion of the H2A α2 helix provides an essential function apart from regulating SWR1 activity, which itself is not essential for viability.
evidence: Inferred from the lethality of the M4 interchange.

claim: SWR1 activity is not essential for viability.
source: This indicates that the N-terminal portion of the H2A α2 helix provides an essential function apart from regulating SWR1 activity, which itself is not essential for viability.
evidence: Based on established knowledge about SWR1.

claim: Glycine 47 is the only surface accessible H2A-specific residue in the M4 region.
source: Glycine 47 is the only surface accessible H2A-specific residue in the M4 region.
evidence: Based on structural analysis of the nucleosome.

claim: Strains bearing single or double amino acid substitutions to corresponding H2A.Z residues-G47K and P49A are viable.
source: Strains bearing single or double amino acid substitutions to corresponding H2A.Z residues-G47K and P49A are viable.
evidence: Supported by experimental data from viability assays.

claim: The single P49A substitution showed no reduction (even an increase) of H2A.Z levels at gene promoters by ChIP-PCR.
source: The single P49A substitution showed no reduction (even an increase) of H2A.Z levels at gene promoters by ChIP-PCR.
evidence: Supported by experimental data from ChIP-PCR shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2B.

claim: The G47K interchange in the M4 region shows reduced H2A.Z incorporation (average 63% of WT).
source: However, the G47K interchange in the M4 region shows reduced H2A.Z incorporation (average 63% of WT), as does the double-substitution G47K, P49A (average 54% of WT), suggesting that G47 facilitates activation of SWR1 in vivo (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data from ChIP-PCR shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2B.

claim: The double-substitution G47K, P49A shows reduced H2A.Z incorporation (average 54% of WT).
source: However, the G47K interchange in the M4 region shows reduced H2A.Z incorporation (average 63% of WT), as does the double-substitution G47K, P49A (average 54% of WT), suggesting that G47 facilitates activation of SWR1 in vivo (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data from ChIP-PCR shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2B.

claim: G47 facilitates activation of SWR1 in vivo.
source: However, the G47K interchange in the M4 region shows reduced H2A.Z incorporation (average 63% of WT), as does the double-substitution G47K, P49A (average 54% of WT), suggesting that G47 facilitates activation of SWR1 in vivo (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: Inferred from the reduced H2A.Z incorporation in G47K mutants.

claim: Specific DNA contacts by ATP-dependent chromatin remodelers are important.
source: Previous studies have established the importance of specific DNA contacts by ATP-dependent chromatin remodelers (Mueller-Planitz et al., 2013; Bartholomew, 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior work.

claim: In vitro, SWR1 is known to bind preferentially to long linker DNA adjacent to a nucleosome core particle.
source: In vitro, SWR1 is known to bind preferentially to long linker DNA adjacent to a nucleosome core particle (Ranjan et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior work.

claim: SWR1 binding to nucleosomes with one 60 bp linker shows protection at superhelix locations (SHLs) SHL0, SHL+1, and SHL+2 on the linker-distal side of the nucleosome dyad.
source: Notably, we observed protection at superhelix locations (SHLs) SHL0, SHL+1, and SHL+2 on the linker-distal side of the nucleosome dyad (Figure 2B,C; Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by hydroxyl radical footprinting data shown in Figure 2B,C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Strongest protection by SWR1 was observed at SHL2.
source: Strongest protection was observed at SHL2, where other ATP-dependent chromatin remodelers have been shown to interact with the nucleosome, but on the linker-proximal or both sides of dyad (Bartholomew, 2014).
evidence: Supported by hydroxyl radical footprinting data shown in Figure 2.

claim: Other ATP-dependent chromatin remodelers have been shown to interact with the nucleosome at SHL2, but on the linker-proximal or both sides of dyad.
source: Strongest protection was observed at SHL2, where other ATP-dependent chromatin remodelers have been shown to interact with the nucleosome, but on the linker-proximal or both sides of dyad (Bartholomew, 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior work.

claim: SWR1 shows broad protection from hydroxyl radical cleavage of long linker DNA.
source: We also observed broad protection from hydroxyl radical cleavage of long linker DNA by SWR1 (Figure 2D), consistent with previous findings (Ranjan et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by hydroxyl radical footprinting data shown in Figure 2D and citation to prior work.

claim: A single gap at −17, −18 nt from the nucleosome dyad blocked the second round of H2A.Z replacement.
source: Systematic introduction of two-nucleotide gaps on one DNA strand of a nucleosome showed that a single gap at −17, −18 nt from the nucleosome dyad blocked the second round of H2A.Z replacement (Figure 3A).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: A 6 nt region (−17 to −22 nt from the dyad) is required for histone replacement.
source: Further scanning identified a 6 nt region (−17 to −22 nt from the dyad), whose integrity is required for histone replacement (Figure 3B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The gap-sensitive region overlaps with the hydroxyl radical footprint of linker-oriented SWR1 at nucleosome position SHL2.
source: This gap-sensitive region overlaps with the hydroxyl radical footprint of linker-oriented SWR1 at nucleosome position SHL2.
evidence: Inferred from comparison of gap-sensitive region and footprinting data.

claim: Introduction of gaps on both sides of the nucleosome dyad caused a complete failure of H2A.Z replacement by SWR1.
source: Introduction of gaps on both sides of the nucleosome dyad caused a complete failure of H2A.Z replacement by SWR1 (Figure 3C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Close contact between SWR1 and nucleosomal DNA around SHL2 is critical for enzyme activation.
source: Taken together, our findings indicate that close contact between SWR1 and nucleosomal DNA around SHL2 is critical for enzyme activation.
evidence: Inferred from the gap-sensitive region and footprinting data.

claim: SWR1 activation likely occurs post-recruitment, as SWR1 binding is not adversely affected on the gap-containing nucleosome substrate.
source: This activation likely occurs post-recruitment, as SWR1 binding is not adversely affected on the gap-containing nucleosome substrate (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: All chromatin remodelers examined to date are able to mobilize positioned nucleosome in vitro, including the strongly positioned 601 nucleosome.
source: To date, all chromatin remodelers examined are able to mobilize positioned nucleosome in vitro, including the strongly positioned 601 nucleosome (Lowary and Widom, 1998; Becker and Workman, 2013; Bartholomew, 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior work.

claim: SWR1 quantitatively evicts both H2A-H2B dimers on the 601 nucleosome, replacing them with H2A.Z-H2B.
source: SWR1 quantitatively evicts both H2A-H2B dimers on this nucleosome, replacing them with H2A.Z-H2B, but whether nucleosome positioning was also altered was unknown.
evidence: Supported by experimental data from histone replacement assays.

claim: Whether nucleosome positioning was altered by SWR1 was unknown.
source: SWR1 quantitatively evicts both H2A-H2B dimers on this nucleosome, replacing them with H2A.Z-H2B, but whether nucleosome positioning was also altered was unknown.
evidence: Based on the authors' knowledge of prior literature.

claim: No substantial mobility shift indicative of a repositioned nucleosome was found after incorporation of (untagged) H2A.Z-H2B.
source: We found no substantial mobility shift indicative of a repositioned nucleosome after incorporation of (untagged) H2A.Z-H2B (Figure 4A).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The INO80 remodeler mobilized the nucleosome from the end- to center-position, as shown by gel mobility shift.
source: By contrast, the INO80 remodeler mobilized the nucleosome from the end- to center-position, as shown by gel mobility shift (Figure 4A) (Shen et al., 2000; Udugama et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A and citations to prior work.

claim: At single nucleotide resolution, there was no net change of the 601 nucleosome position after it underwent one or two rounds of histone H2A.Z replacement.
source: Strikingly, at single nucleotide resolution, there was no net change of the 601 nucleosome position after it underwent one or two rounds of histone H2A.Z replacement (Figure 4C).
evidence: Supported by hydroxyl radical footprinting data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: A DNA site at SHL2 on the nucleosome is important for histone exchange by SWR1.
source: A DNA site at SHL2 on the nucleosome, in a region identified for DNA translocation by chromatin remodelers RSC, SWI/SNF, ISW2, and ISW1, is also important for histone exchange by SWR1.
evidence: Supported by experimental data from gap experiments and footprinting.

claim: SHL2 is in a region identified for DNA translocation by chromatin remodelers RSC, SWI/SNF, ISW2, and ISW1.
source: A DNA site at SHL2 on the nucleosome, in a region identified for DNA translocation by chromatin remodelers RSC, SWI/SNF, ISW2, and ISW1, is also important for histone exchange by SWR1.
evidence: Based on established knowledge from prior work.

claim: The ATPase domains of the SNF2 and ISW2 nucleosome sliding complexes are known to interact with the nucleosome at SHL2.
source: The ATPase domains of the SNF2 and ISW2 nucleosome sliding complexes are known to interact with the nucleosome at SHL2 (Dang and Bartholomew, 2007; Dechassa et al., 2012), and we envision that the catalytic Swr1 ATPase also contacts the SHL2 site.
evidence: Supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The catalytic Swr1 ATPase also contacts the SHL2 site.
source: The ATPase domains of the SNF2 and ISW2 nucleosome sliding complexes are known to interact with the nucleosome at SHL2 (Dang and Bartholomew, 2007; Dechassa et al., 2012), and we envision that the catalytic Swr1 ATPase also contacts the SHL2 site.
evidence: Speculative inference based on analogy to other remodelers.

claim: Other chromatin remodelers contact the nucleosome core particle at either the linker-proximal side or both sides of the dyad axis.
source: Footprinting experiments show that other chromatin remodelers contact the nucleosome core particle at either the linker-proximal side or both sides of the dyad axis; however, SWR1 contacts the core particle on the linker-distal side of the dyad.
evidence: Based on established knowledge from prior work.

claim: SWR1 contacts the core particle on the linker-distal side of the dyad.
source: Footprinting experiments show that other chromatin remodelers contact the nucleosome core particle at either the linker-proximal side or both sides of the dyad axis; however, SWR1 contacts the core particle on the linker-distal side of the dyad.
evidence: Supported by hydroxyl radical footprinting data shown in Figure 2.

claim: The distinction between SWR1 and other remodelers may reflect the unique requirements of dimer eviction and deposition as opposed to nucleosome sliding.
source: This distinction between SWR1 and other remodelers may reflect the unique requirements of dimer eviction and deposition as opposed to nucleosome sliding.
evidence: Speculative interpretation of the observed differences.

claim: Each H2A-H2B dimer is stabilized by histone–DNA interactions at three minor groove locations SHL3.5, SHL4.5, and SHL5.5.
source: Within the nucleosome core particle, each H2A-H2B dimer is stabilized by histone–DNA interactions (at three minor groove locations SHL3.5, SHL4.5, and SHL5.5) and histone–histone interactions (the α2 and α3 helices of H2B interact with α2 and α3 helices of H4 in a four-helix bundle).
evidence: Based on established structural knowledge of nucleosomes.

claim: Each H2A-H2B dimer is stabilized by histone–histone interactions where the α2 and α3 helices of H2B interact with α2 and α3 helices of H4 in a four-helix bundle.
source: Within the nucleosome core particle, each H2A-H2B dimer is stabilized by histone–DNA interactions (at three minor groove locations SHL3.5, SHL4.5, and SHL5.5) and histone–histone interactions (the α2 and α3 helices of H2B interact with α2 and α3 helices of H4 in a four-helix bundle).
evidence: Based on established structural knowledge of nucleosomes.

claim: For histone exchange, SWR1 must disrupt either one or both of histone-DNA and histone-histone interactions, coordinated with H2A.Z-H2B deposition.
source: For histone exchange, SWR1 must disrupt either one or both of these interactions, coordinated with H2A.Z-H2B deposition.
evidence: Logical inference from the structural requirements of histone exchange.

claim: Histone exchange might be initiated by transient, confined DNA translocation by the SWR1 ATPase essentially as indicated for other remodelers, but without propagation as histone exchange is not accompanied by repositioning of the histone octamer on DNA.
source: This might be initiated by transient, confined DNA translocation by the SWR1 ATPase essentially as indicated for other remodelers (Clapier and Cairns, 2009; Mueller-Planitz et al., 2013), but without propagation as histone exchange is not accompanied by repositioning of the histone octamer on DNA.
evidence: Speculative mechanism based on analogy to other remodelers and experimental data.

claim: Histone replacement could be initiated by a local, ATP-driven DNA conformational change near SHL2 that alters the path of the DNA superhelix, resulting in destabilization of H2A-H2B contacts with DNA or with the H3-H4 tetramer.
source: Alternatively, histone replacement could be initiated by a local, ATP-driven DNA conformational change near SHL2 that alters the path of the DNA superhelix, resulting in destabilization of H2A-H2B contacts with DNA or with the H3-H4 tetramer (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Speculative alternative mechanism.

claim: In budding yeast, the +1 nucleosome flanked on one side by a NFR would orient SWR1 to interact with the linker-distal face.
source: In budding yeast, the +1 nucleosome flanked on one side by a NFR would orient SWR1 to interact with the linker-distal face.
evidence: Inferred from the preference of SWR1 for nucleosomes with long linker DNA.

claim: This configuration favors replacement of the H2A-H2B dimer on the NFR-distal side.
source: We speculate that this configuration favors replacement of the H2A-H2B dimer on the NFR-distal side (Figure 2—figure supplement 1, Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Speculative interpretation based on the orientation of SWR1 binding.

claim: Recent genome-wide sub-nucleosomal mapping shows enrichment of H2A.Z at the NFR-distal face of the +1 nucleosome.
source: Consistent with this possibility, recent genome-wide sub-nucleosomal mapping shows enrichment of H2A.Z at the NFR-distal face of the +1 nucleosome (Rhee et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior work.

claim: The structures of H2A- and H2A.Z-containing nucleosomes show prominent differences in the region C-terminal to the histone-fold domain.
source: Earlier work has shown that the structures of H2A- and H2A.Z-containing nucleosomes show prominent differences in the region C-terminal to the histone-fold domain (Suto et al., 2000).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior work.

claim: The C-terminal region is important for binding of the free H2A.Z-H2B dimer to specific chaperones.
source: This C-terminal region is important for binding of the free H2A.Z-H2B dimer to specific chaperones (Luk et al., 2007; Zhou et al., 2008; Hong et al., 2014), and for effector interactions post-incorporation (Clarkson et al., 1999; Adam et al., 2001).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The C-terminal region is important for effector interactions post-incorporation.
source: This C-terminal region is important for binding of the free H2A.Z-H2B dimer to specific chaperones (Luk et al., 2007; Zhou et al., 2008; Hong et al., 2014), and for effector interactions post-incorporation (Clarkson et al., 1999; Adam et al., 2001).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior work.

claim: For histone H2A.Z replacement, SWR1 utilizes unique and conserved features of the H2A nucleosome for substrate specificity.
source: For histone H2A.Z replacement, our analysis shows that SWR1 utilizes other unique and conserved features of the H2A nucleosome for substrate specificity.
evidence: Supported by experimental data from hybrid nucleosome assays.

claim: Of the three SWR1-activating regions of the H2A histone-fold, the α2 helix and loop 2 are exposed on the nucleosome surface for contact with SWR1.
source: Of the three SWR1-activating regions of the H2A histone-fold, the α2 helix and loop 2 are exposed on the nucleosome surface for contact with SWR1, whereas the α1 helix is buried and may act by allostery (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: Based on structural analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3A.

claim: The α1 helix is buried and may act by allostery.
source: Of the three SWR1-activating regions of the H2A histone-fold, the α2 helix and loop 2 are exposed on the nucleosome surface for contact with SWR1, whereas the α1 helix is buried and may act by allostery (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: Speculative interpretation based on structural analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3A.

claim: Residue G47 of the H2A α2 helix is highly conserved.
source: Residue G47 of the H2A α2 helix is highly conserved and is located at the bottom of a cleft (∼8 Å deep) on the H2A nucleosome surface (Figure 1—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: Based on sequence conservation analysis and structural analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3B.

claim: Residue G47 is located at the bottom of a cleft (∼8 Å deep) on the H2A nucleosome surface.
source: Residue G47 of the H2A α2 helix is highly conserved and is located at the bottom of a cleft (∼8 Å deep) on the H2A nucleosome surface (Figure 1—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: Based on structural analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3B.
